adds.title: LGBT rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national 'LGBT rights in Turkey' page is the framework every Turkish province, Osmaniye included, stands under: homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, but there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. Openly LGBTQ people are barred from military service: conscripts who declare their homosexuality are classed under a definition of homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', must provide photographic proof, and risk their 'unfit report' leaking publicly. Same-sex marriage is not recognised, and since 2015 authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years, using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants who defied bans. In 2026 the draft judicial package's LGBTI-discriminatory provisions were removed; the page records a February 2026 press report of a proposed law criminalizing publicly encouraging 'behaviour contrary to biological sex' with one to three years in prison, which was not included in the 2026 omnibus bill (the 12th judicial package).

adds.title: Türkiye - Amnesty International country report (Report 2025/26)
adds.summary: Amnesty International's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26): in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, and over 90 people were arbitrarily detained; prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. In December an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling it had shared 'obscene' images on social media that were incompatible with 'society's moral values' and could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities. The report also records three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people made public during 2025 - an unprecedented assault that would criminalize any expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible to obtain - though they were ultimately not submitted to parliament. In June 2025 the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (Ministry of Health) banned the prescription and supply of hormones for gender-affirming procedures for people under 21.
